summary: Backend-only validation of the URL-only sitemap rewrite. New suite /app/backend/tests/test_sitemap_urlonly.py (11 tests, all passing): preview /sitemap.xml with normal + Googlebot UA, preview /api/sitemap.xml, robots.txt, read-only production report, and a quick admin/catalog regression. Preview static /sitemap.xml returns 200 application/xml, starts with the XML declaration + <urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">, ends </urlset>, parses cleanly, exactly 87 unique <loc> (/, /shop, /about, /contact, /brands + 7 /product-category/*, 8 /brand/*, 67 /shop/<slug>), every url has loc + lastmod (YYYY-MM-DD), all locs https://puff2door.com/, no image: elements, no 'nonaonlinesmokeshop', no query strings, no /cart /checkout /admin /my-account /wishlist /track /order/. /api/sitemap.xml returns 200 application/xml with an identical URL set. robots.txt (Puff2door block) has exactly one Sitemap line = https://puff2door.com/sitemap.xml, no /api/sitemap.xml reference, no blanket Disallow: / for * . Regression: admin login OK, PUT /api/admin/products/<id> with unchanged full payload -> 200, product data unchanged, static frontend/public/sitemap.xml still valid 87-URL image-free XML afterwards, /api/products still 67, home page title correct. Existing test_seo_regression.py (iteration 6) still 11/11 passing. Production is still on the previous deploy (see production_report).

minor.issue: Response sets X-Robots-Tag: noindex. Harmless for the non-submitted API copy, but if this route is ever exposed/submitted as the canonical sitemap, Google may refuse to read it. Consider dropping the header.
lastmod uses container clock (currently 2026-09-03, ahead of real-world date). Future-dated lastmod values are ignored by Google but can look inconsistent; not blocking.

production_report.https://puff2door.com/sitemap.xml: 200, application/xml; charset=utf-8, XML (not HTML), 87 urls, STILL CONTAINS <image:...> tags (previous deploy, expected), first5 = /, /shop, /brands, /about, /contact — both normal and Googlebot UA identical
production_report.https://puff2door.com/robots.txt: 200 text/plain, previous deploy: TWO Sitemap lines (https://puff2door.com/sitemap.xml and https://puff2door.com/api/sitemap.xml); will be single-line after redeploy

action_items: Owner must redeploy so production serves the new URL-only sitemap + single-Sitemap robots.txt; then resubmit https://puff2door.com/sitemap.xml in Search Console (preview content is fully compliant).
Optional: remove X-Robots-Tag: noindex from GET /api/sitemap.xml.
critical_code_review_comments: refresh_static_sitemap() writes into frontend/public at runtime; in the built/production container that directory may be read-only or already baked into the bundle, so the shipped static sitemap is only as fresh as build time. Regenerating at build time (or serving /sitemap.xml through the backend/ingress) would be more robust.

Static /sitemap.xml is served by the frontend build while /api/sitemap.xml is dynamic — they can drift between product changes and the next deploy. Currently identical, worth a scheduled/asserted sync check.
seed_data_creation: None. Admin no-op PUT used an unchanged full payload; product name/price verified unchanged afterwards.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview sitemap rewrite is verified compliant (87 URLs, URL-only). Note: served robots.txt is prefixed by a Cloudflare-managed block containing 'Disallow: /' for AI crawlers (Amazonbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, etc.) — assert only within the '# Puff2door' section. Admin PUT /api/admin/products/{id} requires the full ProductInput body (name, category, categorySlug, price, ...), partial payloads return 422. Production remains on the pre-rewrite deploy until the owner redeploys.
rca_of_the_issue: Original 'Couldn't fetch' was attributed to the non-standard image-extension sitemap referencing external hosts. The rewrite produces a minimal loc+lastmod sitemap that validates against the 0.9 schema and is served as application/xml with 200 for both normal and Googlebot user agents in preview; only a redeploy is pending for production.
